pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Catholic Primary School - Catholic Mission
pageCache.text:
Catholic Mission
"Pupils at St George’s school embrace their mission of faith, embodied in the school motto, ‘In everything we do today, we’re following Jesus and His way.’ Pupils avidly seek opportunities to grow in virtue, pursue the common good and serve those in need..."
To mark World Book Day this year, each class in school chose a book that links to one or more of our Catholic Social Teaching principles. The children listened to the book read during the day and discuss how and why it links to the given principle/s. This is one way in which the children can see how Catholic Social Teaching is woven through different areas of the curriculum. Please see the document below for further information.
Our School House Saints
The Liturgy Team came together to think of ways in which we could further promote the Catholic identity of our school. Building upon a previous initiative which involved each class being given a Saint to mark All Saints Day, the Liturgy team and Leadership team worked together and decided that the children in school will belong to a different ‘house’, each with a designated Saint. Being a part of a Saint’s house reinforces our Mission Statement that we grow together as a family and also helps to nurture a sense of belonging.
When it came to deciding which Saint they’d choose, the children looked at the areas that their Saints are the ‘Patron Saint’ for/of. We also wanted to ensure that there was an equal number of male and female Saints and that they were representative in terms of our diverse community.
We spoke about how it would be nice for the children in each house to come together when it is their Saint’s feast day. We now mark these days with a special Celebration of the Word where children from Reception to Year 6 gather together to hear more about the life of their Saint and to pray for their intercession.
Above our Rosary Garden (via the entrance through the large hall) we have 4 stained-glass windows depicting our House Saints. We used researched a range of imagery to display on the two remaining windows and we chose a dove and a cross. To help the younger children remember which house they are in, each Saint/House has been designated a colour. Each child is assigned a House Saint when they join our school and all siblings belong in the same House. All members of staff, including our Parish priests and Governors, are part of a House.
Bishop John Sherrington blessed these windows when he visited to celebrate Mass for our school’s 80th anniversary.
We look forward to expanding upon this new venture through thinking of the many ways in which we can come together - such as raising money for charities linked to the causes for which our Saints are patrons of and partaking in House-based team activities.
St. Josephine Bakhita: 8th February
St. Thérèse of Lisieux: 1st October
St. Francis of Assisi: 4th October

Welcome from the Headteacher
St George’s, a school known for its warm welcome, calm atmosphere, fantastic academic results and outstanding Catholic education.
On behalf of all the children, staff and Governors, I’d like to warmly welcome you to St George’s Catholic Primary School. We are a popular and successful school recognised for excellence across the curriculum and in the wider education of each child.
As proud providers of a Catholic education we base all relationships on Gospel values and these underpin our daily lives in school. We enjoy close links between school, home and parish and strive to develop the unique potential in every child. The children are guided by their simple but powerful motto: ‘In everything we do today, we are following Jesus and His way.’
We were excited to open our new nursery and new library, both in September 2023. Both are thriving!
We are rated as a good school by Ofsted, and Outstanding in Catholic Life by the Diocese of Westminster. It is my aim as Headteacher to ensure that we are never complacent, and continually strive to improve. I hope that you find our website enjoyable and informative.
Mr P O’Rourke (Headteacher)

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Catholic Primary School - Catholic Social Teaching
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
St George's School recognises the profound impact that embedding Catholic Social Teaching (CST) can have on our pupils. Teachers intentionally plan for elements of CST to be woven throughout the curriculum, ensuring that our children develop a deep understanding of its core principles. Through assemblies, Celebrations of the Word, and cross-curricular learning experiences, our pupils make meaningful connections between CST and their own lives, becoming passionate ambassadors for social justice and change.
By embedding Catholic Social Teaching, nurturing the whole child, building strong community connections, and fostering a diverse, inclusive environment, we are equipping our pupils with the knowledge, skills, and compassion to become agents of positive change in the world. As we follow in the footsteps of Jesus, we are confident that our pupils will continue to make a lasting impact, both within our school and beyond.
Please look through the document below to find out more information about how we proudly teach, promote and live out Catholic Social Teaching at our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Catholic Primary School - Mission Statement
pageCache.text:
Mission Statement
Every Catholic school has a mission statement that encapsulates its distinctive job or core purpose. A mission is a special goal or purpose, one that is accompanied by a strong conviction or calling. At St George’s, a special working party formed of teachers, support staff, governors, parents, clergy and children created the mission statement and it is now displayed throughout the school. It was important that the Mission Statement was meaningful and relevant.
The mission statement puts faith at the heart of all we do at school and incorporates our school motto. It speaks of tolerance and respect that we understand as important Gospel values. Central to a successful education is the relationship between school, home and parish and our mission statement highlights this, as well as building on the success of our Love in Action programme, ensuring a commitment to its positive legacy.

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Catholic Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
"He who sings, prays twice", St Augustine.
Our aim is that all children leave St George's having experienced the enjoyment, engagement and enrichment that music can offer. This can open a wealth of opportunities in secondary school and beyond into later life. We ensure that our music curriculum is broad and meaningful, ensuring that all pupils experience playing a tuned instrument, reading basic musical notation, experiencing live musical theatre and exposure to knowing how local musicians and composers have been influential in the world of music.
Mr Cox is our inspiring music teacher. Using his enthusiasm and experience, he ensures that the national curriculum is fully covered and built upon, creating an exciting curriculum and a wealth of enrichment activities.
Each class has a weekly curriculum music lesson with emphasis on encouraging the children's listening, composing and performing skills. From Year 2 upwards the children have an opportunity to learn to play a musical instrument in the music lesson.
The highlight of many children's journey through St George's is the Year 6 performance in the summer term. Shows such as Aladdin, Matilda and The Lion King have impressed parents and visitors alike.
We currently have individual children learning to play the violin, piano, keyboard and guitar through our partnership with "Enfield Music Service".
St George's also has choirs and a school band.
Singing is also an important part of school life, and this enhances our Celebration of the Word (assemblies), Masses and weekly Hymn Practice. We host a popular singing festival with our partner deanery schools, benefitting from performing and enjoying the experience of singing communally with children from other schools . Yr1 and Yr4 take part in a singing project each year hosted by Enfield Music Service. The children learn vocal techniques and new repertoire culminating in a performance for parents. Each year, children have the chance to experience the thrill of being part of the 'Young Voices' choir at the O2 Arena.

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Catholic Primary School - Science
pageCache.text:
Science
Here at St George’s, we are committed to providing a high quality science education for all pupils. We place a huge emphasis on the development of pupils’ skills in working scientifically. In our science lessons, the skills for working scientifically are taught alongside the scientific content outlined in the National Curriculum.
We encourage enquiring minds and focus on developing the children’s independent scientific thinking. We believe science should be hands-on and fun and where possible integrated with other areas of the curriculum to give a rounded view of the world we live in.
How is Science taught at our school
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum and with relation to science the focus is on ‘Knowledge and Understanding of the World’.
In KS1 and KS2, we follow the National Curriculum whilst also focussing on the key areas of working scientifically: ideas and evidence, planning, obtaining and presenting evidence, considering evidence and evaluating. Within each academic year, children will study a range of scientific topics.
We plan for exciting and stimulating science lessons, using a variety of resources. Pupils are assessed at the end of each topic and these results are used to inform future planning.
Cross curricular learning
Our aim is to teach science and integrate it with other areas of the curriculum. Children are taught how their mathematical calculation and statistical skills can be used to read, analyse and draw conclusions from their results. There are also regular opportunities for children to improve their literacy skills through reading, writing and spelling key vocabulary.
There are also numerous links made with other foundation subjects that are embedded across each science topic.
Mrs J Chambi - Science Subject Leader

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Catholic Primary School - Computing
pageCache.text:
Computing
“A high-quality computing education equips pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world.”
Computing Programme of Study, DfE, 2013.
At St George’s school, we deliver the Computing programme of study for EYFS, KS1 and KS2 with support from the ‘Kapow’ computing scheme of work. The scheme covers all that is required from the Computing programme of study while providing ample opportunity for creativity, collaboration and helping children understand the implications of technology.
We aim for our pupils to achieve a deep understanding of the modern world and the technology that supports it. We wish for all children to be digitally literate and to become a supportive and functioning member of a rapidly changing modern society. We offer an engaging, safe and supportive environment for our pupils to explore and understand different technological mediums such as Interactive Whiteboards, Laptops, Tablets, Computers, Internet, E-mail, Coding, Espresso, DB Primary and much more.
We have two fully functional computer suites that provide children with ample opportunity to learn and explore the capabilities and limitations computing. Each class has access to the large computer suite for an hour a week and our smaller suite is available to smaller groups of children to use for focussed activities. Each phase is also equipped with a standalone computer to support children with regular classroom learning as well as providing opportunities for specific learners to find more accessible ways of accessing the curriculum. We also have a full class set of iPads that can be used for classroom research, stop motion animation, and a range of other activities stretching across the curriculum.
In a rapidly changing society, educating children in online safety is one of our main priorities. We start each new term with a refresher lesson on the do’s and don’ts of staying safe online. We aim to stay abreast of latest changes on social media and technological developments to support children in staying as safe as possible when online.
Mr A Gavas - Computing Subject Leader

pageCache.pageTitle: St George's Catholic Primary School - Geography
pageCache.text:
Geography
“A high-quality geography education should inspire in pupils a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people that will remain with them for the rest of their lives. Teaching should equip pupils with knowledge about diverse places, people, resources and environments, together with a deep understanding of the Earth’s key physical and human processes. As pupils progress, their growing knowledge about the world helps them to deepen their understanding of the interaction between physical and human processes, and of the formation of landscapes and environments. Geographical knowledge provides the tools and approaches that explain how the Earth’s features at different scales are shaped, interconnected and change over time.” National Curriculum 2014
At St George’s school, we deliver the Geography programme of study for EYFS, KS1 and KS2 with support from the ‘Kapow’ Geography scheme of work.
Kapow Primary’s Geography scheme of work aims to inspire pupils to become curious and explorative thinkers with a diverse knowledge of the world; in other words, to think like a geographer. We want pupils to develop the confidence to question and observe places, measure and record necessary data in various ways, and analyse and present their findings. Through the scheme of work, we aim to build an awareness of how Geography shapes our lives at multiple scales and over time. We hope to encourage pupils to become resourceful, active citizens who will have the skills to contribute to and improve the world around them.
The scheme encourages:
Kapow Primary’s Geography scheme of work enables pupils to meet the end of key stage attainment targets in the National curriculum. The aims also align with those in the National curriculum. For EYFS, the activities allow pupils to work towards the ‘Understanding the world’ Development matters statements and Early learning goals, while also covering foundational knowledge that will support them in their further geography learning in Key stage 1.
Mrs L Kyriacou - Geography Subject Leader
